purpose: Check whether the preserved timber pairs already supply a simple direct through-bolted side-lap geometry before selecting an external factory connector.
source_geometry: mini_moonboard.compact_floor_flush_frame.uncut_wood_parts(), current raw timber solids including finished profiles but before new candidate bores
method: For each representative member pair, check exact CAD minimum distance, solid intersection volume, and the opposing bounding end/side datum. Zero overlap alone does not distinguish a lap from a butt; the member identities and end-axis bounds supply the nominal butt interpretation.

pairs.interpretation: The bottom rail terminates against the center principal's x-side. A bolt along the contact normal would be aligned with the long rail direction; no short, accessible head-to-nut path through both members is defined. Oblique bores or added hardware would be new details requiring their own checks.

The center principal starts at the header's top datum; the center clip is also relocated 10.1 mm in y from archived geometry. A direct bolt normal to the butt would enter the principal at its end datum, and no accessible two-member lateral-bolt stack is defined.

The outer side rim starts at the header top datum near retained runner/front-bolt hardware. A direct normal bolt through both members has no selected, accessible full stack or independent moment/separation path.

decision: The existing raw timber geometry does not establish an accessible two-member lateral-bolt detail for these three representative interfaces. Continue a bounded external angle/plate or separately proposed oblique/captive detail; do not apply the existing two-wood-member yield value to an unspecified bolt axis or claim all direct-bolt designs impossible.
